summary: Record, edit, upsert, confirm-forward, and delete a point-in-time value for one account, with the rate permanently stored at entry time as an exact decimal string, provenance tracked (proposed/edited/manual), and a write-then-delete order for a date move onto an occupied date.

read.role: the sweep — Confirm's four rate situations
edit/delete entry point and the two-snapshots-on-one-date fault display
decimal-value typography, the Estimated chip, destructive/replace-confirm conventions, and the shell for the entry, sweep, and detail screens this feature drives

recordShape.value: record_type: "snapshot", account_id set to owner; payload { date, value, rate, rateTarget, rateSource, rateAsOf, proposedRate, note }

decimalRepresentation.value: value and rate are decimal strings, never JSON numbers or floats; parsed to BigInt at fixed scale 12, computed as integers, formatted back to strings

multiplicationRule.value: integer product of two scale-12 values is scale 24, divided back by 10^12 with round-half-even, rescaled exactly once

divisionRule.value: used only in percentage view and per-account interpolation; rounds half-even at scale 12; display rounding is a separate later step

proposedRateSemantics.value: set exactly when rateSource is edited (holds the original proposal, never overwritten by a second edit), null otherwise

rateAsOfSemantics.value: null when manual; for edited it keeps the original proposal's date, unchanged by a later value/note edit

netWorthContribution.value: value * rate, in the main currency

upsertRule.value: one snapshot per (account, date); re-entering an occupied date prompts replace; confirming updates in place (same record_id, version+1, fresh nonce); declining leaves the original untouched

dateMoveOrder.value: moving a snapshot's date onto an occupied date writes the PUT (new date) before the DELETE (displaced record); a failed DELETE leaves both records present rather than losing the displaced one

duplicateDateResolution.value: two snapshots on one date is a reachable, surfaced state: neither is auto-preferred (not highest version, not latest updated_at), both render flagged with a keep-one action, and the date is excluded from interpolation until resolved

editRatePrefill.value: editing opens on the stored rate/rateSource/rateAsOf, never a fresh proposal; editing value/note alone touches no rate field; editing the rate by hand moves proposed->edited and captures proposedRate; changing the date offers (never auto-applies) a fresh proposal

confirmRateRule.value: main currency: rate 1, manual, no request. Live rate source (lookup:true): rate fetched fresh for the new date, previous rate never copied; no proposal -> one-click Confirm unavailable, falls back to manual with previous value prefilled. No rate source (free text or lookup:false): previous rate carries forward, rateSource stays manual

archivedAccountBlocked.value: snapshots blocked against archived accounts except the one closing snapshot written by the archive flow itself (manage-accounts.md)

fixtures: a rounding-midpoint fixture for round-half-even multiplication, exact on the twelfth decimal in both directions
a value with more than twelve decimal places, for the input-rejection criterion
an account measured in XAU-g and one in XAU-ozt, for the 31.1034768 cross-symbol rate assertion
a stubbed rate proxy returning 503, 204, and a differing rate per date, for the manual-fallback, no-proposal-Confirm, and Confirm-fetches-fresh criteria
two snapshots forced onto one (account, date) via a stubbed failing DELETE, for the duplicate-date display and move-order criteria
focus: 'no rate-lookup request contains the entered value, in any field, in any encoding' needs an assertion against the actual outbound request, not just that the endpoint accepts no amount parameter (rate-lookup.md already covers the server side; this is the client's discipline)
the write-then-delete move order must be proven with a stubbed failing DELETE showing both records still exist, not just asserted from the spec text
the duplicate-date criterion requires the client to pick neither record and exclude the date from interpolation — verify both halves, not just that both rows render
editing a value alone must assert the rate proxy received zero requests, not just that the stored rate field is unchanged

the round-trip decimal criteria ('0.1' + '0.2' = '0.3') must run through the actual BigInt scale-12 arithmetic path, since a float-based reimplementation would also happen to pass a naive string-equality check on simple inputs
